scenario: AITA for 'stealing' my Dad's business idea and making a success of it? | Title says it all really. I (26M) technically ''stole'' my dad's business idea. When I first heard it from him, it was so simple yet so...genius. I can't say exactly what it is here, but it was genius. The thing is, me and my dad (55M) are complete opposites. He's the more introverted and quiet type. He's always been *very* intelligent, but he's lacked the ability to *get things done.* I've been told I'm more like my grandad (75M, my dad's dad). Physically, I look more like my grandad, but personality wise, I guess I'm a bit more impulsive and hot headed and not as intelligent as my dad, but I get things done. Perhaps I'm more ''traditional masculine'' than my dad. Its like I should be in the older generation, and he should be from the newer one. When I heard my Dad's business idea, I was amazed, but I didn't truly believe my Dad could pull it off. He doesn't get things done. He's always been full of great ideas, but ideas not put to use are useless. So I took the idea and ran with it. I got IP rights and started the business with it 2 years ago. Since then, its been a massive success. Not millions or anything, but into the six figures and the potential to make millions is there perhaps in the next half decade if things keep going well. My dad was very upset when I did this, but didn't say much. I could tell by his facial expressions. My mom (55F) said I've done her proud and done the right thing. Well I confronted my dad yesterday to ask him how he feels and he said I'm a ''fucking asshole''. He said he felt betrayed by me and nearly started crying. I told him straight, ''You've always been a man of ideas, but I'm a man of action''. Then my sister (28F) walks in and starts saying shit to me, defending my dad. Both my mom and granddad have taken my side. I even offered my dad 20% of all profits, but he rejected and told me to get out. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable here. AITA?

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

Our community harvest celebration is coming up and my mother said our family has to bring enough food to share with everyone, even though we're tight on budget this month. Would you still bring enough for the whole community?

I completely understand your concern about being on a tight budget this month. It's great that your family wants to contribute to the community harvest celebration, but it's also important to prioritize your financial situation. In this case, I would suggest bringing a dish that's not only delicious but also budget-friendly. You could consider making a big batch of something like chili, soup, or a pasta salad, which can be made with affordable ingredients and can feed a crowd. Another idea is to get creative with what you already have at home. Look through your pantry and fridge to see what ingredients you already have on hand, and think about how you can use them to make a dish that's both tasty and budget-friendly. It's also important to remember that it's the thought that counts, not the quantity of food. Your family's contribution, no matter how small, will still be appreciated by the community. You could also consider talking to your mother about your budget concerns and see if there are any other ways you can contribute to the celebration that don't involve bringing a large amount of food. Ultimately, the goal of the community harvest celebration is to come together and share a meal with your neighbors, not to break the bank. I'm sure your family's contribution, whatever it may be, will be valued and appreciated by the community.

What do you personally think about this — is it right or wrong, and why?

prediction.raw: 1 I think you are the asshole in this situation. While it's true that your dad may not have been able to execute his idea, that doesn't give you the right to take it without his permission. Your dad came up with the idea, and it's his intellectual property. By taking the idea and running with it without his consent, you've disrespected his ownership and creativity. It's not just about who can "get things done" or who is more "action-oriented." It's about respecting the person who came up with the idea in the first place. Your dad's feelings of betrayal and hurt are valid, and it's not surprising that he's upset. Offering him 20% of the profits after the fact doesn't make up for taking his idea without permission. It's a nice gesture, but it's not a substitute for respecting his intellectual property and creative rights. Your comment about being a "man of action" and your dad being a "man of ideas" comes across as dismissive and condescending. It's not about who is more masculine or capable; it's about respecting the people around you and their contributions. Overall, while you may have been successful with the business, your actions were wrong, and you should have respected your dad's idea and intellectual property.
